content: Candesartan cilexetil has minimal impact on aldosterone secretion and does not significantly affect serum potassium levels. In hypertensive adults, multiple-dose studies revealed no clinically significant changes in metabolic parameters, including serum levels of total cholesterol, triglycerides, glucose, or uric acid. In a 12-week study involving 161 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, there was no change in HbA1c levels. In heart failure patients, doses of candesartan ≥8 mg led to reductions in systemic vascular resistance and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure. Candesartan exhibits high plasma protein binding (>99%) and does not penetrate red blood cells. The protein binding remains constant even at plasma concentrations exceeding those achieved with recommended doses. Animal studies in rats indicate that candesartan crosses the blood-brain barrier poorly, if at all. However, it does cross the placental barrier and is distributed to the fetus. When administered orally, approximately 26% of the dose is excreted unchanged in the urine. Following an oral dose of radiolabeled candesartan cilexetil, about 33% of the radioactivity is recovered in urine and 67% in feces. After an intravenous dose of radiolabeled candesartan, approximately 59% of the radioactivity is recovered in urine and 36% in feces. Biliary excretion contributes to the elimination of candesartan. In adults, candesartan cilexetil is rapidly and completely bioactivated to candesartan, a selective AT1 subtype angiotensin II receptor antagonist, via ester hydrolysis during gastrointestinal absorption. Candesartan is primarily excreted unchanged in urine and feces (via bile) and undergoes minor hepatic metabolism through O-deethylation to an inactive metabolite. The elimination half-life of candesartan is approximately 9 hours. Its pharmacokinetics are linear for oral doses up to 32 mg, and neither candesartan nor its inactive metabolite accumulates in serum with repeated once-daily dosing. The absolute bioavailability of candesartan is estimated to be 15%. Peak serum concentrations (Cmax) are reached 3 to 4 hours after tablet ingestion, and high-fat meals do not affect its bioavailability. In pediatric patients aged 1 to 17 years, plasma levels of candesartan are more than 10-fold higher at peak (approximately 4 hours) than at 24 hours after a single dose. A dose of 2 mg/kg in children results in exposure similar to that in adults receiving 8 mg. Children older than 6 years exhibit exposure levels comparable to adults given the same dose. Pharmacokinetics (Cmax and AUC) are not influenced by age, sex, or body weight. However, the pharmacokinetics of candesartan cilexetil have not been studied in pediatric patients under 1 year of age. Dose-ranging studies indicate a dose-related increase in plasma candesartan concentrations. The renin-angiotensin system (RAS) plays a critical role in kidney development, and RAS blockade has been shown to cause abnormal kidney development in very young mice. Therefore, children under 1 year of age must not receive candesartan. Drugs acting directly on the RAS can disrupt normal renal development. In elderly patients (≥65 years), plasma concentrations of candesartan are higher compared to younger subjects, with Cmax approximately 50% higher and AUC approximately 80% higher. However, the pharmacokinetics remain linear in the elderly, and neither candesartan nor its inactive metabolite accumulates in serum with repeated once-daily dosing. No initial dosage adjustment is necessary in elderly patients. There is no difference in the pharmacokinetics of candesartan between male and female subjects. In hypertensive patients with renal insufficiency, serum concentrations of candesartan are elevated. The pharmacokinetics in hypertensive patients undergoing hemodialysis are similar to those in patients with severe renal impairment. Candesartan cannot be removed by hemodialysis. No initial dosage adjustment is required in patients with renal insufficiency. In heart failure patients with renal impairment, AUC0-72h was 36% and 65% higher in those with mild and moderate renal impairment, respectively.
